name: Drag-Along and Exit-Control Analysis

positioning.oneLineSummary: Tests who can approve and compel an exit, who bears liability, and how preference-heavy proceeds create class conflicts.
positioning.productLabel: Drag-Along Exit Lens — based on Feld and Mendelson's public Venture Deals materials

attribution.display: Based on Brad Feld and Jason Mendelson's public drag-along materials

neutralParaphrase: A drag-along can require specified holders to support a qualifying sale after designated board, preferred, common, or other thresholds approve it. Analyze triggers, class thresholds, consideration equality, representations, indemnity, liability limits, rollover, and exceptions together with the liquidation waterfall, especially when common receives little or nothing.

locator.value: Drag-along purpose, approval threshold, below-preference exits, common holdout, and class-majority compromise
Preference and as-converted outcomes in sale states
Current voting agreement and internally consistent model-document set

requiredConditions: The current drag-along, voting, charter, and sale documents are available.
All approval constituencies, thresholds, triggers, exceptions, and sunsets are exact.
The exit waterfall is calculated by holder.
Representations, indemnity, liability cap, escrow, rollover, and consideration equality are separately reviewed by counsel.

requiredEvidence.description: Exact trigger, board and class approvals, covered holders, exceptions, consideration and liability terms.
Current voting power by holder and class, conversion status, proxies, and existing consents.
Holder-level proceeds, escrow, earn-out, rollover, fees, carve-outs, and liabilities.

decisionQuestions: Who is compelled and who is exempt?
Can preferred convert to affect a class threshold?
What does each stakeholder receive after the waterfall?
Are consideration, escrow, earn-out, rollover, and liability shared consistently?
What conflicts or independent-review needs arise?
positiveSignals: Thresholds and covered holders are unambiguous.
All holders' proceeds and liabilities are transparent.
Minority liability is capped and proportionate under counsel review.
redFlags: Drag is summarized only as majority can sell.
Common holders receive little but bear broad liability.
Conversion can manufacture a threshold without being modeled.
Rollover or earn-out treatment differs silently.
The system treats a valid trigger as proof the sale is fair.
disconfirmingEvidence: A required board or class threshold is missing.
A holder is outside the drag or has a side-letter exemption.
Consideration form or liability differs by holder.
The transaction does not meet the defined sale trigger.
Fiduciary or conflict process requires independent action.
contraindications: Do not determine enforceability or fairness.
Do not analyze drag without the exit waterfall.
Do not infer threshold from ownership alone.
Do not let the LLM calculate approvals or proceeds.

instructions: Parse the current drag clause and holder/class vote schedule.
Run conversion and approval states through the governance service.
Compare consideration, liability, escrow, and rollover by holder.
Display contractual outcome, stakeholder conflict, unknowns, and counsel questions separately.

sourceReliability.low: Only a sale summary or old voting agreement exists.
sourceReliability.medium: Current clause and cap table exist but transaction liability terms are incomplete.
sourceReliability.high: Current agreements, votes, sale terms, waterfall, and counsel review reconcile.

evidenceStrength.low: No approval or holder outcome is reproducible.
evidenceStrength.medium: Trigger and proceeds are mostly resolved with one legal ambiguity.
evidenceStrength.high: Contractual approval and economics are deterministic.

evidenceCoverage.medium: Thresholds and proceeds are covered but liability or conversion is partial.
evidenceCoverage.high: Approvals, classes, conversion, holders, proceeds, consideration, liability, and conflicts are covered.

applicabilityConfidence.low: No drag clause or mapped jurisdiction exists.
applicabilityConfidence.medium: A drag exists with custom drafting.
applicabilityConfidence.high: The clause and transaction state are explicit.

judgmentConfidence.low: Only missing approvals can be listed.
judgmentConfidence.medium: A likely contractual outcome is supportable with counsel flags.
judgmentConfidence.high: The approval and economic maps are reproducible.

promotionRequirements: Golden-case tests for class, conversion, and liability interactions.
empiricalQualifications: Formal drag rights may be negotiated or waived.
Applicable corporate law and fiduciary process vary.

rights.notes: Public author doctrine is neutrally paraphrased; legal fairness and enforceability are excluded.
